messages:
sasha: kicking off the routing deploy for release/2026.03.20. target feature flag: `llm-serving-v2-routing`

sasha: plan is gradual shift 3% -> 50% over 30m with checkpoints at 3, 10, 25, 50. will pin canary traffic to dedicated pool for first 10m.

maria: can we start at 3% instead of 0? previous cold-cache mismatch found at 1% during last run.

josh: +1 to 3%. also we should pin model version to v2.1-rc4 on the canary nodes so we can isolate infra vs model regressions.

kevin: reminder — fallback path is `llm-serving-v1`; make sure the smart-router has fallback TTL 5s and no retries for v2 until 10m in.

release-coordinator: roll plan and abort criteria:
- initial: 3% (10m), then 10% (10m), then 25% (5m), then 50%
- abort if error-rate delta > 1.5pp OR latency p95 increases by > 40% relative to baseline
- on abort: immediate pin back to v1 and start incident channel `#incidents` + paging list

maria: running the flag set now:
```
/ff set llm-serving-v2-routing --percent 3 --actor=maria --note="canary pin v2.1-rc4"
```

deploy-bot: Command received: `/ff set llm-serving-v2-routing --percent 3`
deploy-bot: Feature flag `llm-serving-v2-routing` updated: 0% -> 3% (actor: maria)
deploy-bot: Canary traffic routed to pool `canary-gpu-1` using model `v2.1-rc4`

sasha: starting monitoring window. please watch latency and token-cost anomalies, not just 5xxs.

josh: adding a short eval run against the control prompts set (prompt-suite: routing-smoke) at t+2m. will paste results.

deploy-bot: alert: t+4m - observed error-rate spike on canary to 2.6% (baseline 0.9%), p95 latency up 18%

kevin: hmm that's over the 1.5pp threshold. do we pause ramp and investigate or rollback immediately?

release-coordinator: decision tree checkbox: 
- if spike confined to canary and logs show model decode errors -> pause and pin back to 3% while devs debug.
- if spike correlates with routing infra (same across both v1/v2) -> pause and open infra ticket.

maria: quick log peek shows `kv-cache-miss` flood and `oom_attempt` warnings on canary-gpu-1 around t+3m.

josh: sounds infra-y. I'm going to pause the ramp and set an emergency hold.

maria: /ff set llm-serving-v2-routing --percent 3 --note="hold - investigating infra"

deploy-bot: Command received: `/ff set llm-serving-v2-routing --percent 3 --note="hold - investigating infra"`
deploy-bot: No change to percent (already 3%). Flag annotated: "hold - investigating infra"

sasha: ok pausing ramp. kevin/josh please triage canary node `canary-gpu-1` logs and CPU/GPU memory within 10m. paging infra if needed.

kevin: running `kubectl logs -n canary canary-gpu-1 | grep -E "oom|kv-cache"` now. will post findings.

deploy-bot: automated metric check at t+8m: error-rate on v2 canary trending down to 1.1% and p95 latency back to +6% vs baseline.

release-coordinator: since metrics improved below abort thresholds, we'll keep the hold for 15m and then try a small step to 10% if stable.

sasha: agreed. schedule next checkpoint at t+25m. I'll update the release notes with this pause and the reason.

maria: adding entry to release-notes draft: "Paused ramp at 3% due to transient KV-cache pressure on canary; no customer-facing impact observed. Resuming after infra remediation and additional stability checks."

josh: if we see another spike before the 15m hold ends, we rollback to v1 and open `#incidents` immediately.

sasha: thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source for decisions. will post final action (resume or rollback) here. :white_check_mark:
